title: EngineRunManifest
description: One (engine, model) cell's execution record for the engine-performance layer (docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Every accuracy or latency result row must carry one of these so a delta can be attributed to engine/quantization/sampling/hardware rather than left ambiguous. Accuracy and latency passes for the same cell are two separate manifests (separate runs), never one.

run_id.description: Unique per execution, e.g. ULID. Distinct from case id.

pass_type.description: Which pass produced this manifest. An accuracy sweep and a latency pass over the same cell are never the same run (eval_bench/repetition.py's n=5 shuffle sweep is itself a load generator and would corrupt its own timing numbers). accuracy_under_load is the concurrency-vs-correctness probe (docs/engine-performance-plan.md 'なぜこの層を足すのか' > 並行負荷下でのツールコーリング精度維持) -- kept as its own pass_type rather than reusing 'accuracy' with cell.concurrency set, so its concurrency=1 control point and high-concurrency point are never silently pooled with the plain accuracy sweep's implicit concurrency=1 baseline.

engine.description: transformers_hf is the naive baseline (no serving-level batching). ollama is optional/deprioritized: it wraps llama_cpp's inference core, so engine deltas against llama_cpp may be near-null and must be reported as such, not hidden.

tool_catalog_version.description: The top-level 'version' of whichever catalog file backed this run. Determined by tool_stage, not by pass_type: tool_stage=10 must reference schema/tools.json's version (the original 40-tool catalog, identical to Article 1's), tool_stage=50/100 must reference schema/tools_extended.json's version (the 100-tool catalog: the same 40 plus 60 added for this layer, generated by scripts/generate_extended_catalog.py). Never compare results across different catalog versions at the same nominal stage -- the tool sets, and therefore selection difficulty, differ.

model.description: 8B-class model id/name, pinned to a specific checkpoint (see docs/engine-performance-plan.md's model-size decision).

quantization.description: e.g. 'gguf-q4_k_m', 'awq-4bit', 'fp16-none'. Must be held equivalent across engines being compared in the same cell pair; if an engine can't match, exclude that cell rather than silently adjusting.

tool_stage.description: Shared by both accuracy and latency pass_type: [10, 50, 100] (see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Stage 10 uses ONLY the original 40-tool catalog (schema/tools.json) -- same tools dict Article 1 uses, so results overlay Article 1's own stage=10 numbers exactly. Stages 50/100 use the extended 100-tool catalog (schema/tools_extended.json: original 40 + 60 added for this layer, same ERP domain, same module structure -- deepened existing modules and/or plausible additional ERP modules, e.g. production/project management; not confusability-engineered like the original 40, but must be genuinely plausible business tools, not generic placeholders, per external precedent (tau-bench, BFCL, ToolBench all scale within a coherent domain rather than mixing unrelated ones) -- obviously-synthetic filler risks teaching the model an 'ignore oddly-named tools' shortcut that would distort the very large-catalog effect this stage is meant to measure). Passing the extended dict for a stage=10 run would change the padding candidate pool and break the Article-1-overlay property -- must not be done.

prompt_layout.description: Ordering of the stable prefix (system prompt + tool schema + few-shot) versus the variable query within the prompt. stable_first (query last) maximizes prefix-cache hit rate under each engine's default-on caching (vLLM V1 and llama.cpp server's cache_prompt are both enabled by default -- an ON/OFF toggle was rejected as unrealistic, see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). query_first breaks the cache for everything after the query since prefix caching matches from the start of the sequence. Unlike a pure cache toggle, this CAN affect correctness (position bias / lost-in-the-middle), so it is required in both accuracy and latency manifests, not latency-only. transformers_hf has no serving-level cache, so its latency should be ~layout-invariant -- that null result is itself the control point.

concurrency.description: Number of requests fired concurrently. 1 = serialized (the attribution-safe default). >1 is only meaningful for engines with request-level batching (vllm; llama_cpp's --parallel slots are a fixed-reservation approximation; transformers_hf has no request scheduler or shared KV at all and is excluded from the concurrency axis entirely, reported at concurrency=1 only as the no-serving-optimization control point -- see docs/engine-performance-plan.md). Required for pass_type latency and accuracy_under_load; must be absent for plain pass_type accuracy, which is concurrency=1 by convention and never states it explicitly (see the allOf rule forbidding it below).

instance_type.description: e.g. 'g6.xlarge'. Fixed across all cells in this plan so hardware is never a confound -- see docs/engine-performance-plan.md.

repetition.description: Required when pass_type == accuracy; mirrors eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated's shape.

results.description: Shape depends on pass_type; see the allOf below.

allOf.$comment: query_first is an ablation, not the accuracy baseline: docs/engine-performance-plan.md scopes it to the largest tool_stage only, to keep the layout axis one-factor-at-a-time instead of tripling the full accuracy sweep.

Plain accuracy manifests are concurrency=1 by convention (docs/engine-performance-plan.md: 'accuracy pass is concurrency=1 for all engines'). Forbid stating cell.concurrency at all here so a concurrency-under-load data point can never be mistaken for -- or silently pooled with -- the plain sweep's baseline; that probe is pass_type accuracy_under_load instead.

warmup_excluded.description: Warmup requests must always be excluded from reported percentiles.

allOf.$comment: The concurrency-vs-correctness probe (docs/engine-performance-plan.md > 並行負荷下でのツールコーリング精度維持). Scoped to vllm + awq-4bit (layer 2): bf16 (layer 1) leaves too little VRAM headroom under non-shared-prefix conditions to reach a meaningful high-concurrency point, see docs 'KVキャッシュブロッカーの解消'. Both the concurrency=1 control point and the high-concurrency point for this probe use this same pass_type, distinguished from each other only by cell.concurrency -- never pooled with plain accuracy's implicit concurrency=1 baseline.

accuracy_results_base.description: Shared by pass_type accuracy and accuracy_under_load -- both are eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated output, differing only in which cell fields are legal (see the allOf branches above) and in whether vllm_diagnostics is a defined property.

arg_exact_mean.description: Null iff no case in this stage/model had exact-scored fields to evaluate. Computed by eval_bench.repetition.aggregate_repeated, pooled over only the trials where the metric was applicable (selection succeeded on a positive case with scoreable fields of this kind).

vllm_diagnostics.description: Populated whenever cell.engine == 'vllm' and cell.concurrency > 1. vLLM does not OOM when KV capacity is exceeded -- it queues excess requests -- so a concurrency>1 manifest without this cannot be trusted to reflect true concurrent batching rather than serialized queueing delay reported as if it were throughput (docs/engine-performance-plan.md 'KVキャッシュブロッカーの解消'). Not schema-required (transformers_hf/llama_cpp never populate it, and it would be vacuous at concurrency=1) -- the execution harness is responsible for refusing to write a concurrency>1 vllm manifest without it, and for discarding a run where observed_max_concurrency < cell.concurrency.

gpu_blocks_reported.description: vLLM startup log's '# GPU blocks', for audit.

observed_max_concurrency.description: vLLM startup log's 'Maximum concurrency for N tokens per request', evaluated at this cell's tool_stage context length. Must be >= cell.concurrency or the run measured queueing delay, not concurrent batching, and must be discarded rather than reported.
